name: Christian right
summary: The Christian right is a politically conservative Christian, mainly American evangelical, movement that seeks to shape law and public life by biblical moral values. Its core causes are banning abortion, defending the traditional family and opposing same-sex marriage, public prayer and religion in schools, and support for Israel, usually together with free-enterprise, pro-military Republican conservatism.
scope: The US Christian right from the Moral Majority and 1980 Reagan-era coalition through the Christian Coalition and later evangelical political activism. Economic and foreign-policy answers are mostly inferred from the Republican platform it allied with; non-American Christian-democratic or social-gospel strands are excluded.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The movement allied with Reagan-era conservatism, whose platform declares war on overregulation and upholds free enterprise.

public-ownership.rationale: Platform defends free enterprise and private property and calls for deregulation; public ownership is opposed.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The 1980 platform backed across-the-board income tax cuts and opposed higher taxes.

property-fundamental.rationale: The platform calls private property foundational to free enterprise and the republic.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The platform declares war on government overregulation of business, though the movement favours regulating media and pornography.

cut-welfare.rationale: The platform backs removing ineligibles, block grants to states and rejects a guaranteed income; dependency is a common conservative theme.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The movement opposes drug use and supports drug prohibition, and the platform pledges to curb illegal drugs with mandatory sentences.

strong-leader.rationale: Adherents are split; the movement has backed strong figures like Reagan and Trump but also prizes constitutional limits.

state-harmful.rationale: The movement wants government to enforce moral order and defence; the state is not seen as harmful in itself.

limit-guns.rationale: The platform says the right to keep and bear arms must be preserved and opposes federal gun registration.

empower-police-military.rationale: The platform calls for a major upgrade of the military and tougher crime policy including the death penalty.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The movement opposes pornography and sexual immorality and seeks to restrict them by law.

decide-locally.rationale: The platform stresses returning welfare to states, but the movement also seeks national constitutional amendments on abortion and marriage.

rehabilitation.rationale: The platform stresses deterrence and mandatory sentences rather than rehabilitation.

traditional-family.rationale: Promoting traditional family values is a founding purpose; the platform calls the family the foundation of the social order.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The Moral Majority opposed state recognition of same-sex relationships and the movement opposes LGBT rights.

abortion-legal.rationale: Opposing abortion is the movement's defining cause, including the 1980 call for a personhood amendment and overturning Roe.

more-religion-public.rationale: The movement seeks public prayer, Bible and Ten Commandments in schools and a larger public role for Christianity.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The movement upholds a traditional, creation-based view of sex and gender and opposes second-wave feminism and LGBT claims.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Defending traditional, Christian American culture and values is the movement's aim.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not defining; the platform opposes aid to illegal aliens, but evangelical views on immigration are split.

nation-first.rationale: Aligned with American conservatism's sovereignty emphasis; not a defining statement.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Adherents split between hawkish internationalists and sceptics; the movement has campaigned over persecuted Christians abroad.

central-planning.rationale: Platform defends free enterprise and deregulation.

basic-income.rationale: The platform categorically rejects a guaranteed annual income.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not a defining issue; adherents are split; the movement never took a position on this, so the answer rests on its general conservative outlook.

separate-church-state.rationale: The movement campaigns for school prayer, vouchers for religious schools and Bible teaching in public curricula (s1, s2), each a rejection of strict separation; its own sources reject a strict wall rather than state an alternative doctrine.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Adherents want law to reflect biblical morality on abortion, marriage and sexuality, but most stop short of full scriptural law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The platform backs law enforcement and a stronger military as state functions.

military-superiority.rationale: The platform calls for a major upgrading of military forces; the Moral Majority opposed SALT.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Rejects Marxist materialism; sees history in providential or moral terms.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Platform rejects guaranteed income and quotas.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Christian ethic stresses charity and duty, though it defends free enterprise.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Adherents emphasise both moral duty and constitutional liberties.

limit-population.rationale: The movement is pro-natal and opposes abortion and contraception-based population control.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The movement opposed embryonic stem cell research and prioritises moral limits.

human-enhancement.rationale: The movement opposes embryonic stem cell research and bioethics changes it sees as violating human dignity.

restore-past-order.rationale: The movement frames its work as recovering traditional moral order against secular change.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Moral principle is placed over pragmatism; the movement never took a position on this, so the answer rests on its general conservative outlook.

direct-action.rationale: The movement mobilises through elections and lobbying.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The platform defends free enterprise and private property.

taxation-theft.rationale: Favours tax cuts but not that taxation is theft.

harm-principle.rationale: The movement seeks to restrict adult conduct on moral grounds such as pornography, drugs and sexuality.

media-academia-power.rationale: The Moral Majority opposed media seen as anti-family and the movement targets secular universities and media.

total-state.rationale: Platform seeks limited government and deregulation.

national-rebirth.rationale: The movement speaks of moral renewal of a nation seen in decline.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The movement criticises supposedly neutral secular education, yet claims objective truth.

universal-morality.rationale: Adherents hold moral truths grounded in God and Scripture that bind all cultures; whether reason alone suffices is debated.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Evangelical Christian Zionism holds Israel's restoration fulfils biblical prophecy; support is a prominent movement feature.

school-vouchers.rationale: The movement has backed school vouchers since the 2010s; the platform backed tuition tax credits.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The platform opposed balancing budgets through taxes yet sought spending restraint; fiscal conservatism is typical.

economic-freedom.rationale: Aligned with free-enterprise conservatism; the movement never took a position on this, so the answer rests on its general conservative outlook.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Adherents ground belief and action in faith and Scripture.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The platform called for ending aid to illegal aliens.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The platform sought removing ineligibles and the voluntarily unemployed from welfare rolls.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-10): its rationale says most adherents do not seek law imposing the roles, so the sources cited here do not answer this statement.

reviewHistory.rationale: The movement opposed the ERA and upholds distinct family roles, but most do not seek law imposing them.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-10): its rationale says most adherents do not seek law imposing the roles, so the sources cited here do not answer this statement.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Mainstream movement does not advocate legal segregation; the platform condemned busing quotas but not integration itself.

national-mission.rationale: The movement often sees America as a providential Christian nation.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The movement opposes second-wave feminism and rejects this analysis.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Opposed on pro-life and human-dignity grounds.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The movement wants a state that also enforces moral law and supports the family.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Christian doctrine of human dignity is central to its pro-life framing.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Christian Zionism rejects this view of Israel.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The movement is evangelistic; the Moral Majority proselytised.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The movement supports school prayer and Bible instruction in public schools.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Adherents split between biblical concern for the poor and fiscal conservatism.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Distrust of supranational bodies and nationalism.

clerical-rule.rationale: The movement works through elected government; no clerical rule.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The movement opposes pornography but typically frames this as obscenity law rather than censoring art; adherents split.

death-penalty.rationale: The 1980 platform says the death penalty is an effective deterrent; some pro-life Christians dissent.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The movement has campaigned for abstinence-only sex education and against gender-equality curricula.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The movement supports creationism in public school textbooks and opposes teaching evolution alone.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Opposing pornography is a long-standing battle of the movement.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The movement campaigns for religious-liberty protections for believers against laws that conflict with faith, though it frames the claimant as Christian rather than as a minority.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Evangelicals favour charity and missions but split on government aid; no stated platform line.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The 1980 platform calls for military strength and a strong defence, from which an independent US deterrent follows.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The movement's Christian Zionism rests on a biblical claim to the land of Israel, which supports keeping it.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Defending religious liberty and church independence from the state is a founding cause of the Moral Majority and the movement.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Adherents favour limited, decentralised government but no view is stated on a region's separate legal and economic system.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Biblical Christianity reserves holiness for God, so a ruler regarded as sacred or divine would be idolatry.

equal-parenting.rationale: The movement stresses fathers and the traditional family but does not take a clear position on custody presumptions.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The movement backs patriotic, Christian-leaning education and has fought school curricula it sees as undermining American heritage, as in its creationism and school-prayer campaigns.

patriotic-education.rationale: The movement stresses faith, flag and country, and the 1980 platform and Moral Majority back patriotic values in schools.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The 1980 Republican platform it shaped opposes quotas and preferences, and the movement backs colour-blind policy.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not an issue for the movement; American conservatives are split on influence over former British lands, and the movement is not linked to imperial succession.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Adherents are split: they defend religious owners' freedom to refuse service, yet they backed civil rights law and moral regulation of businesses.

elective-rulers.rationale: Elective government is assumed; the movement is Republican and constitutionalist.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement is defined by political mobilisation of believers; the Moral Majority urged participation.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The movement favours free enterprise and rejects dependency theory.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Not a founding value for the movement, which regards its founding sources as Christian.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The movement is strongly anti-communist, and its criticism of totalitarianism was a Cold War staple; the 1980 platform is the basis.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The movement and the Republican alliance defend national monuments and heritage.

filial-duty.rationale: The movement stresses the traditional family and the biblical command to honour parents, as in its pro-family agenda.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Communal or use-based land tenure contradicts the private-property, free-enterprise stance of the Republican platform it supported.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The movement is pro-family and pro-life and favours tax relief for families, as the 1980 platform does, rather than immigration for demographics.

job-guarantee.rationale: The 1980 platform it helped shape favours private-sector job growth and tax cuts over government employment programmes.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The movement defends the traditional family and opposes recognition of same-sex relationships and the erosion of legal marriage.

informal-organisation.rationale: The movement built formal organisations such as the Moral Majority and the Christian Coalition and works through the Republican Party.

religious-nation.rationale: The movement seeks to shape public life by Christian values and treats America as a Christian nation, but it formally accepts religious liberty.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Not a defining issue; adherents are split between states'-rights keep-your-revenue views and a national party line.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The 1980 Republican platform it backed defends free enterprise and private property against collectivism.

defeat-communism.rationale: Anti-communism was a founding cause of the Moral Majority and the 1980 platform.

religion-illusion.rationale: The movement holds that religion answers lasting human needs and seeks to build law on biblical values.

socialized-care.rationale: The movement defends the traditional family and opposes state take-over of child rearing.

cooperative-communities.rationale: A free-enterprise, pro-family movement rejects common-property communities as a model.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Christian Zionism grounds support for Israel in a biblical covenant tie to the land, which the movement treats as weighty.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The movement allied with the Republican platform, which defends free elections and constitutional liberties; it organises through open political competition.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The movement opposes LGBT rights and opposes legal recognition of gender identity along with same-sex marriage.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The movement seeks to shape law by biblical moral values, treating morality and authority as ultimately from God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The 1980 platform and Moral Majority demand school prayer and more religion in public life, opposing a ban on religious expression.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The 1980 platform calls for a strong military, and the movement is pro-military.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The movement backed Reagan's assertive Cold War stance and an Israel alliance, so it favours alignment, not neutrality.

online-participation.rationale: The movement uses online mobilisation but has no stated position on internet deliberation and decisions.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The movement holds to biblical authority and traditional moral teaching, and defines itself against modernising reinterpretation of scripture.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The Moral Majority campaigned against gay rights and for traditional morality, so open gay service would be opposed.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The movement defends religion in public life and opposes secularism, so state-promoted atheism is rejected.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The 1980 Republican platform stressed law and order and support for police, which the movement allied with.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The 1980 platform and the movement favour private and church-based charity over government welfare.

rent-control.rationale: The 1980 Republican platform stood for free enterprise and deregulation, which the movement allied with.

recognise-genocide.rationale: No common movement position; adherents are split between support for recognition and indifference.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The movement backs a strong military, the death penalty and a right to self-defence, so it rejects absolute pacifism.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The movement upholds traditional sex roles and opposes the gender-theory view, so rejects that sex is socially constructed.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The movement frames politics as a culture war over biblical morality and a defence of Christian values against secularism.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Christian Zionism sees Israel as a prophetic homeland, but there is no common view on a diaspora cultural centre.

god-not-male.rationale: Conservative evangelicals hold that God is revealed in male terms, such as Father and King.

arms-reduction.rationale: The 1980 platform called for military strength and the Moral Majority opposed SALT II arms-limitation efforts.

capital-controls.rationale: The 1980 platform backed free enterprise and open markets, and the movement allied with the Republican free-market line.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The movement is strongly pro-military and patriotic, as in the 1980 Republican platform it allied with, so refusing orders is rejected.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Adherents want a moral blueprint for society but free markets in economics; no stated position.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Its opposition to abortion and bioethics rests on a created, fixed human nature with inherent dignity.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Evangelical exclusivism holds that salvation is through Christ alone, rejecting the view that all religions share one truth.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The Republican platform the movement backed demanded military strength and opposed unilateral disarmament.

premarital-sex.rationale: The Moral Majority and the movement campaigned for traditional sexual morality, treating sex outside marriage as sinful.

women-suffrage.rationale: Movement women and men take part in electoral politics, and no mainstream Christian-right body opposes women voting or holding office.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The movement defends traditional Christian family roles and sees religion as a support to women and family, not a cause of oppression.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The Moral Majority and the wider movement were built on fundamentalist and evangelical Christians who treat the Bible as inerrant.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The movement shared the Republican platform's strong anti-communism and its rejection of planned socialist economies.

national-church-status.rationale: The movement seeks a role for religion in public life but, as a mostly evangelical coalition in the US, does not seek a privileged state church.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The movement backs the death penalty only after due process and defends life and legal order, so killing without trial is rejected.

self-ownership.rationale: Its opposition to abortion and drug use rests on moral duties to God and life, rather than unlimited rights over one's body.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The movement supports free enterprise and rejects Marxist economics as part of its anti-communism.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The movement ties patriotism to Christian values and the Republican coalition, and it draws on working-class evangelical voters.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The movement opposes communism, as the Moral Majority's anti-SALT and anti-Soviet agenda shows.

missingStatements.text: Public schools should teach creationism or intelligent design alongside evolution.
missingStatements.rationale: The movement supports creationism in public school textbooks and opposes teaching evolution alone.

missingStatements.text: Pornography should be restricted by law.
missingStatements.rationale: Opposing pornography is a long-standing battle of the movement.

missingStatements.text: Public schools should allow organised prayer.
missingStatements.rationale: Both the 1980 platform and the Moral Majority call for school prayer.

notes: Evangelical views on immigration, trade, the death penalty and the poor are split, and most economic answers are inferred from the allied Republican platform.
